analysis:
The units are head-side excerpts of docs/provider/cli-reference.md, a documentation-only change with no executable code. I examined them against the threat model for TB-011, TB-012, TB-013 and TB-014, and A-008 and A-018.

Relevant statements:
- The logout text (lines ~880-929) says the saved token is sent as a Bearer credential to the issuer recorded in owner-only metadata. It follows no redirects, uses a 10 s timeout, and counts only HTTP 204 as confirmed revocation. Offline logout is reported as unconfirmed. This matches the A-008 and T-053 descriptions and weakens no control.
- The switch/models_replace text describes fail-closed behavior and the need for a coordinator upgrade. It adds no new trust boundary beyond what the doc states.
- The cluster gpu-limit section (lines ~690-709) states that a confirmation and a macOS administrator prompt are required. That is consistent with TB-014 and T-062.
- The patch excerpt shows the sandbox row now requires approval from a waitlist for `setup`. This tightens access to the TB-013 surface and does not widen it. The waitlist enforcement itself is not visible in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm it.
- The prefix-cache and benchmark text says the paged-Qwen rollout is not yet validated and that benchmark selection is not release evidence. That does not overclaim.

I found no concrete security regression. The documented behaviors are implemented in Swift source and in the platform, and neither is supplied. The patch excerpt is truncated and the changed ranges (head 1360-1385, 1635-1724) fall beyond the supplied text, so the added content there was not reviewed. Integration should check that the docs for the waitlist gate and the hold/mailbox features match the code. A doc claim is not proof of enforcement.
